signals.long_summary: Listen Labs, a startup led by Alfred Wahlforss, faced significant challenges in hiring over 100 engineers against intense competition from large companies like Facebook, which was offering substantial salaries. To address this, the company employed a unique approach through a viral billboard hiring stunt, successfully raising $69 million to scale their operations focused on utilizing AI for customer interviews. This innovative strategy highlights creative recruitment methods in a competitive job market and underscores the impact of novel marketing tactics in attracting talent and funding. For a community aiming to stay informed about AI, such developments demonstrate the intersection of technology, entrepreneurship, and talent acquisition strategies in the evolving landscape.

signals.title: Anthropic launches Cowork, a Claude Desktop agent that works in your files — no coding required
signals.summary: Anthropic released Cowork on Monday, a new AI agent capability that extends the power of its wildly successful Claude Code tool to non-technical users — and according to company insiders, the team built the entire feature in approximately a week and a half, largely using Claude Code itself. The launch marks a major inflection point in the race to deliver practical AI agents to mainstream users, positioning Anthropic to compete not just with OpenAI and Google in conversational AI, but with Microsoft's Copilot in the burgeoning market for AI-powered productivity tools.

signals.title: Mitigating Database Leakage in RAG Systems with Keyword-Grounded Fact Substitution
signals.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for combining large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge sources. However, RAG systems remain vulnerable to prompt injection attacks, which may mislead the retriever or generator to expose sensitive database contents.

signals.title: Let Credit Follow Computation: Architecture-Aware Credit Transport for Large Language Model Reinforcement Learning
signals.summary: Credit assignment in large-language-model reinforcement learning (LLM RL) can be separated into three objects: evidence about success, a transport operator that converts this evidence into token-level advantages, and an update geometry that turns advantages into policy changes. Recent work has greatly improved evidence, sampling, and update geometry, but the transport operator is usually architecture-agnostic.

signals.title: AIREP: A Protocol for Per-Decision Evidence in AI Runtime Governance
signals.summary: A protocol is presented for recording the governance decisions of automated AI runtimes. When a runtime releases, blocks, defers, redacts, or escalates an individual output, AIREP records that decision as a single signed object that any party can check offline, independent of the runtime that produced it.

signals.title: Salesforce rolls out new Slackbot AI agent as it battles Microsoft and Google in workplace AI
signals.summary: Salesforce on Tuesday launched an entirely rebuilt version of Slackbot , the company's workplace assistant, transforming it from a simple notification tool into what executives describe as a fully powered AI agent capable of searching enterprise data, drafting documents, and taking action on behalf of employees. The new Slackbot, now generally available to Business+ and Enterprise+ customers, is Salesforce's most aggressive move yet to position Slack at the center of the emerging "agentic AI" movement — where software agents work alongside humans to complete complex tasks.
